macro.text: Dow futures −234 (−0.5%) on Home Depot, S&P flat, Nasdaq-100 +0.5% after Monday's S&P −1.9% and Nasdaq −2.5%; Nvidia reports after the bell.
A projectile hit a tanker in Hormuz; Iran says four tankers struck mines and calls the southern route closed; a third U.S. carrier arrived. Brent 93.16 (+0.8%), WTI 86.36 (+0.8%) on the price feed.
10-year 5.118%, 30-year 5.472%, 2-year 4.806% (−2 bp); dollar index 103.60. October retail sales at 8:30 AM (Forex Factory: 0.1% headline, 0.4% core); a December hike is fully priced (Movers Report).
Nvidia warned buyers of legal risk over Chinese remote access to its chips after Commerce's interim rule Monday; it won't sell to clouds renting over 50% of GPUs to Chinese firms.

The FCC-led block on new Chinese optical transceiver models advances despite Amazon, Google, Meta and Microsoft lobbying; Chinese vendors hold ~2/3 of the market. COHR +9%, LITE +5%, GLW +3% premarket.
Citadel's Rubner: realized equity volatility is the highest since April 2025; SPY's average daily move of 1.3% is double its one-year average. Kospi −2.6%, Nikkei −1.3% overnight.

briefs.read: Mixed open: QQQ +0.4% (664.32), SPY flat (739.84), IWM −0.3% premarket; VIX 22.83. Chips bounce before Nvidia reports tonight; retail sales at 8:30 AM. Monday's opening bounces faded all day, so wait for the 15-minute range and a retest before trusting any break.

briefs.flowNote: Money is coming back into chips and growth premarket after Monday's rout: semiconductors (SMH +1.3%), high-growth tech (ARKK +1.1%) and technology (XLK +0.8%) lead, helped by the optical names on Reuters' report of a block on Chinese transceivers and positioning before Nvidia tonight. It is leaving the defensives that led last month: health care (XLV −1.0%; LLY −1.3%, HUM −3.3%), staples (XLP −0.7%) and materials (XLB −1.5%), with consumer discretionary (XLY −0.5%) dragged by Home Depot. Over 5 days and a month chips are still the worst group (SMH −5.2%, −15.8%), so this is a bounce inside a downtrend, not yet a rotation.

bigPicture: Everything waits on Nvidia tonight: its first report under interim CEO Kress, with the stock ~35% off its October high and options pricing ~7%, the most since February 2025.
Policy is splitting AI hardware: Commerce's rule on Chinese remote access weighs on Nvidia's buyers, while a planned block on Chinese transceivers lifts U.S. optical makers.
Rates still cap the rebound: the 10-year at 5.12% and a fully priced December hike, with retail sales today and the FOMC minutes Wednesday.
The defensive bid is fading: health care and staples are the weakest premarket after Monday's late give-back, and volatility is the highest since April 2025 (Citadel).
snapshot.takeaway: Monday's lesson stands: every AI bounce into its gap edge in the first 15 minutes faded all day. Today's chip bounce comes before Nvidia's report and right after retail sales, so let the first 15 minutes set the range and treat anything open at 4 PM as an earnings bet.

sectors.text: NVDA +1.2%, AMD +1.9%, MU +1.3%, AVGO +1.1% after Monday's −4% to −8%; INTC −0.7% after Nvidia cut its stake by 25%. New China remote-access rules hang over Nvidia's buyers. The report tonight decides direction; the bounce is positioning.

Reuters says the block on new Chinese optical transceivers is moving ahead: COHR +9.2%, LITE +5.1%, GLW +2.8% (Jefferies starts Buy, $134), ANET +2.4%. No effective date yet, and all four are below their 50 EMA.

CRWV +1.4% (50.59) after Monday's −6.1%; NBIS −0.6%; ORCL +0.2%. Nvidia's ~$36B of neocloud backstops and its new rule on renting GPUs to Chinese firms are tonight's questions; a 5.12% 10-year keeps the funding worry alive.

IGV −0.1%: MSFT −0.4%, PLTR +0.3%. The Anthropic IPO is expected to price this week, a supply event for the group; I'm built by Anthropic, so treat it only as a sector catalyst. Palo Alto reports Wednesday.

Brent 93.16 (+0.8%), WTI 86.36 (+0.8%) after a projectile hit a tanker in Hormuz and Iran claimed four mine strikes, but XLE is flat premarket after −2.0% Monday; the IEA's Q4 surplus view and OPEC+ on Nov 29 cap it. CVX nears a ~$5B Gulf deal (FT).
